text.p: Casinos Austria International Ltd (CAIL) said on Wednesday chief executive officer Alexander Tucek had stepped down on June 30 as part of management and board changes.

Tucek, who had been appointed by CAIL's parent to head other projects, would also relinquish his position as a director of CAIL and a director of Reef Corporate Services Ltd, CAIL said in a statement.
General manager operations Heinz Resmann had also resigned and would return to Vienna-based Casinos Austria AG, which owns 67 percent of CAIL.
CAIL in March reported a net loss of A$18.47 million for calendar 1996, due mainly to a write-down in its investment in the Reef Casinos Trust, which owns the troubled Reef Casino in Cairns.
CAIL said it expected conditions to remain difficult in 1997.
The company said on Wednesday its new board would consist of an executive chairman, an executive director and three non-executive directors.
CAIL's chairman Ben Macdonald had been appointed executive chairman and would assume control of the company.
Thomas Jancik, a senior executive of Casinos Austria, had been appointed executive director.
